description: Local fixes to Bitwarden's Vault Management API spec, applied by upstream/spec_fixes.py to upstream/vault-management-api-original.json to produce upstream/vault-management-api-fixed.json. Paths name their target by key and, for array elements, by selector; see upstream/README.md.

fixes.value: Request schema for unlocking the vault with master password

fixes.why: The url filter takes any URI, not only an http(s) URL; `url` is not an OpenAPI string format, `uri` is.

The body is a bare JSON array of collection ids, as the spec's own description and example say: bw serve passes it straight to ShareCommand.run, which iterates it as string[] (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, apps/cli/src/admin-console/commands/share.command.ts). Upstream describes it as an object with an `array` property, so the model rejected the example.

value.name: permanent
value.description: Delete the item permanently instead of moving it to the trash.

fixes.why: bw serve accepts `permanent` on item deletes (the CLI's delete command reads it for items only), but the spec does not document it. Decided on #21.
The master password is a secret; `password` format makes its model field a SecretStr, so it never shows in a repr. Decided on #30.
On /unlock the message embeds the new session key (`export BW_SESSION=...`); `password` format makes it a SecretStr. On /lock it is null. Decided on #30.
bw serve returns the session key as `raw` on /unlock (the spec's own example shows it) but the schema does not declare it; declared as a SecretStr. Decided on #30.

The example spells the field `externalid`; the collection schema and CollectionExport (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, libs/common/src/models/export/collection.export.ts) spell it `externalId`, so the example was wrong, not the model.

The device approval example carries organizationUserId, and PendingAuthRequestResponse sends it (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, bitwarden_license/bit-cli/src/admin-console/device-approval/pending-auth-request.response.ts), but the schema omits it, so the response model dropped it.

The CLI accepts item types 1-8: CipherType is Login=1, SecureNote=2, Card=3, Identity=4, SshKey=5, BankAccount=6, DriversLicense=7, Passport=8 (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, libs/common/src/vault/enums/cipher-type.ts; bitwarden/sdk-internal 4a9eb239 (0.2.0-main.1126, the version the CLI pins), crates/bitwarden-vault/src/cipher/cipher.rs). 6-8 are behind a server feature flag, and CreateCommand answers them with a 400 when it is off (apps/cli/src/vault/create.command.ts). Upstream lists only 1-4, so SSH keys and the newer types were refused (#108).

fixes.value: Type of vault item (1=login, 2=secure note, 3=card, 4=identity, 5=SSH key, 6=bank account, 7=driver's license, 8=passport)
fixes.why: Names the item types the enum now allows (#108).

A card's brand is free text: CardExport declares `brand?: string` and encrypts it as-is (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, libs/common/src/models/export/card.export.ts), and the SDK's Card holds `brand: Option<String>` (bitwarden/sdk-internal 4a9eb239 (0.2.0-main.1126, the version the CLI pins), crates/bitwarden-vault/src/cipher/card.rs). Upstream allows only `visa`, the value in the CLI's own template, so every other brand was refused (#108).

A field's type is a number: FieldType is Text=0, Hidden=1, Boolean=2, Linked=3 (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, libs/common/src/vault/enums/field-type.enum.ts; bitwarden/sdk-internal 4a9eb239 (0.2.0-main.1126, the version the CLI pins), crates/bitwarden-vault/src/cipher/field.rs, serialized as a u8). Upstream declares it a string with integer values, so the model was a plain Enum rather than an IntEnum (#108).

GetCommand.getTemplate also answers item.bankaccount, item.driverslicense and item.passport (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, apps/cli/src/commands/get.command.ts), with a 400 while the new item types' feature flag is off. Upstream omits them (#108).

CipherExport.toView copies `type` unchecked on create and edit (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, libs/common/src/models/export/cipher.export.ts), so an item without one reaches the SDK with no type, the path where an unknown type takes bw serve down (#108).
See the fido2Credential component (#108).

OrganizationCollectionRequest takes `users?: SelectionReadOnly[]` beside groups (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, apps/cli/src/admin-console/models/request/organization-collection.request.ts), and `bw get template org-collection` returns it, so a template posted back was refused (#108).

SelectionReadOnly has `manage` beside readOnly and hidePasswords (bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, apps/cli/src/admin-console/models/selection-read-only.ts), and the org-collection template carries it (#108).

The CLI copies `disabled` unchecked (SendResponse.toView, bitwarden/clients cli-v2026.10.1, apps/cli/src/tools/send/models/send.response.ts) and Vaultwarden answers a Send without it with 422 (recorded: send-create-no-disabled). False is the CLI's own template value, so it is sent by default rather than required (#108).
